propositions: A failed or timed-out tickets-branch fetch causes init to silently create an empty divergent orphan store instead of failing closed.
The branch-mount predicate only checks local refs and cannot distinguish a genuinely absent remote branch from an unreachable remote.
A shared tri-state remote-branch probe using git ls-remote --exit-code distinguishes advertised, reachable-absent, and unreachable, and is consumed by all four init consumers.
Unreachable or timed-out remotes must fail closed with a distinct diagnostic naming remote, branch, and timeout, never creating an orphan unless override supplied.
A --force-new-store flag and force_new_store keyword authorize deliberate bootstrap only when reachability is unknown, and is ineffective (warns) when the remote is reachable.
The tri-state probe result is cached under a short TTL keyed by repo, remote, and branch so one CLI invocation performs at most one probe on the unreachable path.
